name: Evaluation Datasets
blurb: Benchmarks and test sets, and what each actually measures.

items.note: Grade-school math word problems; the standard arithmetic-reasoning test
Science exam questions in easy and challenge splits
57-subject knowledge exam; the most-cited general capability benchmark
The successor suite to GLUE for language understanding
Commonsense sentence completion designed to be adversarial to models
164 hand-written programming problems; the original code-generation benchmark
The harder ten-choice successor as frontier models saturated MMLU
Graduate-level science questions that resist search; gated to keep answers out of training data

reading.body:
GSM8K leads all nine benchmarks with 1.17 million downloads, nearly double MMLU's 606,000, which signals that arithmetic reasoning is the most actively tested capability in current evaluation practice.

The download counts reveal a clear ordering: mathematical and factual knowledge tasks attract far more use than language-understanding suites or code generation. MMLU-Pro exists specifically because frontier models saturated MMLU, and its 204,000 downloads suggest the field is already cycling toward harder replacements. GPQA, gated to prevent its answers from leaking into training data, sits at the bottom of the download ranking with 121,000, which partly reflects access friction rather than lack of interest.

None of these datasets measure compute directly, and download counts say nothing about which benchmarks actually drive model development decisions versus which are run after the fact for reporting. What the data does show is that the evaluation layer is heavily concentrated: nine openly accessible datasets, most under permissive licences, constitute the shared vocabulary of capability measurement across the field. When those benchmarks saturate, as MMLU demonstrably did, the community produces harder successors rather than retiring the practice of standardised testing.
